Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Identify needs
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Production and Dissemination Specialist' (EC-05) is responsible for investigating client requirements for statistical information, defining project objectives and priorities, and determining sources of data for special requests (e.g., 'Investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used.'). This includes modifying existing techniques or developing new approaches to meet specific needs, integrating data from various sources, and providing expert advice to users inside and outside the organization. Future GSBPM expectation: The future state of 'Identify needs' demands that staff proactively scan all existing data holdings and alternative data sources first, and employ rigorous cost-benefit, timeliness, and risk assessments before initiating any new data collections or surveys. There is an explicit expectation for solution-oriented thinking, automation, reuse, and documentation to support digital workflows, with new data collection being a last resort, justified only as necessary. Role evolution: The EC-05 role will need to evolve from responding to client needs with a survey-first or special study mindset, toward leading a thorough digital/data asset discovery, leveraging internal and external data, and systematically validating if a new collection is required. Decision-making will become more evidence-based, documented, and digitally traceable, with a requirement to challenge default assumptions and construct robust business cases for new surveys. Earlier and more formalized stakeholder engagement will include feasibility, automation, and AI considerations. Capability implication: Greater importance will be placed on in-depth knowledge of data sources (internal, administrative, external), digital navigation skills for metadata-assisted data discovery, the ability to conduct and document cost-benefit-risk analyses, an understanding of automation and AI readiness, and the capability to communicate and justify complex, resource-driven decisions to both clients and internal governance.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Consult and confirm needs
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist is responsible for investigating client requirements for statistical information, defining the nature and scope of special studies, and determining sources of data for special requests and studies. As per the work description, they 'provide subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC' and 'knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide advice on program results.' These responsibilities inherently include the consultation and confirmation of stakeholder needs and translating these into statistical products.

Future GSBPM expectation: The future-state for consulting and confirming needs shifts from a focus on initiating new data collection to a model in which existing and alternative data holdings are examined first, leveraging AI-supported platforms and automated discovery tools. Consultations will be more rapid, iterative, outcome-driven, and will emphasize transparent assessment of trade-offs, value, and reusability, with new survey launches being a last resort following explicit, documented justification and cost-benefit analysis.

Role evolution: The EC-05 role will shift from lengthy, exploratory consultations toward facilitating joint assessments of user needs via digital platforms that highlight available holdings and trade-offs. Rather than defaulting to proposing special studies and custom surveys, the specialist will guide stakeholders through the possibilities and limitations of what can be delivered from current assets, using shared metadata and automated tools to evaluate feasibility, timeliness, and value. The role will also require structured documentation and explanation of decision pathways, rationale for rejecting new survey initiation, and negotiation based on the organization’s prioritization criteria. Interactions with clients will be more frequent, agile, and will require real-time, data-driven dialogue.

Capability implication: The new emphasis on data discovery and automated consultation platforms demands much deeper knowledge of agency data holdings, advanced facility with digital data discovery and metadata tools, and fluency in facilitating transparent discussions around data quality, fitness-for-use, value trade-offs, and cost-benefit within fast-paced, outcome-focused cycles. A greater understanding of automated decision support systems, AI-augmented discovery tools, and the rationale for prioritization based on organizational strategy will become vital for effective performance in the redefined consultation process.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Establish output objectives
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist plays a critical role in defining project objectives and priorities, preparing work plans outlining approaches, timeframes, and resources, and determining sources of data for special requests or studies. This includes deciding whether to use existing data sources or to initiate new collection efforts (see: 'Investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used.'). The Specialist also interprets user needs, integrates data from various sources, and negotiates with system specialists, methodologists, and clients regarding resources, timeframes, and costs.

Future GSBPM expectation: In the future state, establishing output objectives will require defaulting to the reuse of existing data holdings and demonstrating the infeasibility of meeting needs through alternative or administrative data before proposing new survey activity. Objectives must also embed automation, machine-readability, and interoperability as standard requirements, with explicit digital execution constraints in place from the outset. Resource discipline and a justification-based approach to any manual or custom methods are now front-loaded in the acceptance of objectives.

Role evolution: The EC-05 will need to shift from responding flexibly to client or user needs with bespoke or survey-based solutions, to proactively justifying all proposed data sources and methods within the context of digital-first, automation-enabled, and resource-efficient workflows. The role's responsibility for defining project objectives will be more tightly intertwined with demonstrating compliance with agency-wide automation, interoperability, and reuse criteria, requiring more structured evidence and documentation, and more direct collaboration with IT and data governance experts upfront. The determination of data sources and methods now involves systematic assessment of digital and operational feasibility, not just subject-matter relevance.

Capability implication: As a result, this role will increasingly depend on deep knowledge of internal data assets and agency data architecture, applied understanding of automation and interoperability requirements for output design, digital evaluation techniques, and the frameworks for cost-benefit analysis as applied to statistical output scoping in a digital context. Evaluating trade-offs among reuse, automation, survey scope, and digital scalability will become essential to this role's effectiveness.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Identify needs
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Head, Production and Dissemination' (EC-06) plans and implements long-term program strategies, develops policies, assesses program requirements, and reviews the conceptual framework for statistical programs (e.g., 'Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs.'). The position is responsible for determining data acquisition methods, assessing trends, and integrating data from various sources, often including data not originally collected for current purposes. Future GSBPM expectation: The revised 'Identify needs' phase now serves as a strategic enterprise-wide gatekeeper, with a proactive obligation to scan all data assets for reusability, assess operational feasibility of new collections, and apply dynamic cost/timeliness/risk trade-offs. This function is essential to realizing StatCan2030’s objectives for efficiency, digital enablement, and resource optimization. Role evolution: This leadership role will shift toward enforcing digital-first, cross-program data asset utilization and implementing standardized needs identification procedures supported by digital platforms (e.g., data inventories, risk/cost tracking tools). EC-06 incumbents must drive this culture change and ensure that proposals for new projects include thorough, auditable documentation of needs assessment, alternative data explorations, and automation-readiness. They will increasingly participate in resource trade-off decisions, digital workflow alignment, and must build and reinforce mechanisms for early, digitally-enabled stakeholder engagement. Capability implication: This elevates the importance of strategic data asset management expertise, awareness of digital and AI technologies for discovery and automation, advanced understanding of cost/risk frameworks, and the ability to champion cross-organizational change toward digital, sustainable statistical production.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Consult and confirm needs
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination, plans and implements strategies for statistical programs, prepares program proposals, develops policies and guidelines, and provides expert advisory and consultative services to users. The position involves 'investigating client requirements for statistical information and determining the capacity and ability of existing or modified systems to meet these requirements,' and requires knowledge of key client department policies to identify and respond to information needs. The current approach supports both custom development and adaption of existing methods/products in response to evolving client demand, often in a consultative, iterative fashion.

Future GSBPM expectation: In the future-state, program launch and needs confirmation become highly evidence-driven, prioritizing reuse, automation, and cost efficiency. Strategy and program decisions will require explicit resource alignment and justification for any new data collection, with consultations underpinned by shared, transparent platforms tracking needs, commitments, and trade-off decisions. The role expands into stewardship of the consultation ecosystem: ensuring staff leverage digital tools, that process cycles are short and trackable, and that agency prioritization (what gets built) is transparent and defensible. Decision-logging and metadata-driven alignment are integral parts of this expectation.

Role evolution: The Head’s responsibilities will move toward embedding real-time consultation support mechanisms, monitoring and guiding the adoption of digital platforms for needs consultation, and defining the boundary conditions for when new collections are justified. Leadership will shift away from supporting exploratory program expansions to enforcing a rigorous structure of reuse-first, feasibility-driven, and transparently documented consultations. Accountability will include tracking consultation timelines, overseeing trade-off and cost-benefit deliberations, and ensuring continuous process improvement through feedback loops captured in shared tools.

Capability implication: This creates a heightened need for expertise in digital product/platform development for stakeholder consultation, oversight of automated and AI-augmented consultation workflows, advanced resource optimization, and knowledge of performance analytics for process cycles (timeliness, reuse rates, rejection/acceptance of new data collection proposals). Deep understanding of policy, strategic prioritization, and the mechanisms for effective, transparent trade-off discussions will be necessary, as well as change management proficiency to shepherd the workforce through these operational and cultural shifts.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Establish output objectives
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination is responsible for planning and implementing long-term strategies for statistical programs, developing and recommending frameworks, policies, and guidelines, and preparing program proposals outlining statistical frameworks, strategies, and resource implications ('Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs.'). The Head also defines the methods and practices for data acquisition, production, and dissemination, and manages the evaluation of new data sources and systems for their feasibility and program impact.

Future GSBPM expectation: The future-state output objective establishment process is considerably redefined: it mandates that objectives prioritize asset reuse, automation-readiness, digital and resource efficiency, and interoperability by default, with demonstrable justification for any custom/manual or survey-first approaches. Approval for output objectives thus shifts toward an investment-style gate, tightly linked to enterprise architecture, automation pipelines, and digital resource limitations.

Role evolution: The EC-06 will now need to ensure all program and project proposals systematically demonstrate adherence to reuse, automation, and interoperability gates before advancing, integrating enterprise architecture and IT conversations into the earliest scoping and objective-setting decisions. This role will lead in formalizing processes and criteria for objective acceptance, establishing requirements for automation, and enforcing resource and feasibility discipline. It will require more structured collaboration across program, subject-matter, IT, and data governance leads to present business cases for any non-standard output.

Capability implication: The change elevates the importance of strategic data asset stewardship, deep alignment with enterprise IT and automation standards, and the capability to analyze, synthesize, and communicate cost-benefit and digital feasibility arguments at the program acceptance stage. The Head must also be able to balance statistical relevance with digital architecture constraints, and audit or establish processes for evaluating output proposals against agency-wide, automation-first priorities.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Identify needs
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer' (EC-04) develops and implements statistical processing systems, designs data specifications, and conducts feasibility studies for new systems and projects, often collaborating across divisions (e.g., 'Conducts feasibility studies concerning new system and product requirements by examining existing, proposed or new software programs and systems to determine their feasibility and adaptability to the needs of the statistical program.'). The role also negotiates procedural modifications, provides guidance on subject-matter requirements, and analyzes current methods for relevancy and improvement. Future GSBPM expectation: Needs identification must now precede all project proposals with structured digital scanning for existing data and explicit operational feasibility analyses, considering digital, AI, and automation capabilities from the outset. System enhancements or new data collections must be justified by documented inability to fulfill requirements with existing assets. Role evolution: The officer's work will move from mainly evaluating the technical fit of new requirements in the context of system development, to actively engaging in a standardized, enterprise-driven needs identification funnel. This means greater responsibility for conducting and documenting data asset and system audits, collaborating with business intelligence tools for rapid discovery, and steering feasibility assessments that incorporate automation, digital workflow compatibility, and sustainability perspectives. Capability implication: Increasingly critical are capabilities in digital inventory navigation, understanding of metadata standards and federated data sourcing, and operationalizing cost-benefit-risk analysis at the systems and process design stage, as well as synthesizing this information for formal project decision points.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Establish output objectives
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer develops processing systems, designs specifications for testing and maintenance, and assesses subject-matter changes and their impact on methods, systems and program results. This includes participation in translating user or program requirements into systems specifications and operational project plans, as well as leading teams in the implementation of new or modified systems ('Assesses changes in the subject area and determines the need to modify or replace processing systems and applications for the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data').

Future GSBPM expectation: The future state necessitates that output objectives, and by extension any supporting system or operational plan, are justified for re-use, automation, and interoperability at inception. The Officer's assessments must now include not just technical feasibility, but digital alignment, resource constraints, and explicit elimination or justification of custom/manual or new data collection methods wherever possible, with digital system integration as a primary criterion.

Role evolution: The EC-04 will need to actively embed automation, interoperability, and reuse principles into all initial assessments, modifications, and systems designs. Their project proposals and system specifications must provide evidence of compliance with digital priorities and resource discipline before advancing, and they will need to negotiate and translate these constraints in interaction with subject-matter and IT stakeholders from the outset. Instead of accommodating user-driven custom solutions by default, they now enforce digital supply chain standards upfront and help develop the rationale for exceptions.

Capability implication: This evolution makes knowledge of agency data holdings, automation frameworks, digital integration constraints, and the rationale for cost/efficiency trade-offs crucial. The role’s analytical focus will shift toward digital system design thinking, interoperability certification, and resource-justification frameworks within output objective-setting, in addition to subject-matter and statistical methodology.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Identify concepts
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-04 is accountable for developing subject-matter concepts and definitions, leading system development, and addressing problems in the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of statistical information. Relevant to concept identification, they 'develop subject-matter concepts and definitions', 'propose new statistical methods, techniques and approaches', and negotiate procedural modifications in collaboration with users and colleagues. The current method is iterative and expert-driven, grounded in reaction to subject area changes or user requests.

Future GSBPM expectation: With automation and interoperability prioritized, the initial identification of concepts shifts to system-guided exercises leveraging AI and metadata. The EC-04’s input is needed for validating, contextualizing, or justifying deviations from enterprise standard concepts, often in compressed timelines and collaborative, cross-program contexts.

Role evolution: The EC-04’s decision-making shifts from conceptual authorship towards arbitration, solution vetting, and the alignment of program content with enterprise frameworks. The officer will lead or participate in review teams working with automated discovery tools, and engage more rigorously in cross-domain prioritization and conflict resolution to ensure enterprise-wide reusability and compliance.

Capability implication: Increased emphasis falls on architectural understanding of statistical concepts, enterprise-level negotiation, identifying when and how to adjust automated suggestions, and awareness of the digital frameworks and metadata repositories that drive automation and harmonization at scale.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Identify needs
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator' (EC-03) coordinates data retrieval, validation, and dissemination; recommends and implements changes to improve statistical systems and processes; and acts as a subject-matter liaison for user requirements (e.g., 'Identifies and assesses trends and developments in the subject area; reviews the potential impact on program subject-matter content and determines the implications for statistical methods and procedures.'). The role involves interpreting user requests, identifying sources of information, and analyzing and recommending modifications to current data collection and processing approaches. Future GSBPM expectation: With needs identification becoming an upfront, digital-first, and cross-program responsibility, the coordinator is expected to perform proactive scans for data reuse, contribute to cost and timeliness analyses, and rigorously document the rationale for new collections. Engagement with clients and data users becomes more structured and evidence-based, relying on digital tools to assess the feasibility and sustainability of meeting statistical needs. Role evolution: EC-03 incumbents will transition from a largely responsive approach to user requests, to a proactive gatekeeping and diagnostic role, systematically leveraging agency data assets, automation capabilities, and digital discovery tools before escalating requests to new projects. They will need to integrate operational feasibility and digital readiness assessments into their workflow, and record rationales in standardized formats supporting automation and audit. Capability implication: Emphasized will be knowledge of digital data inventories, metadata-driven search and evaluation, process documentation for audit and design handover, and the ability to synthesize and communicate operational constraints and readiness for automation to both internal stakeholders and clients.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Consult and confirm needs
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-03 Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator coordinates the retrieval, validation, and dissemination of data, provides custom tabulations for ad-hoc client requests, and 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development.' Other key duties include interpreting user requests, determining feasibility, and advising on subject-matter concepts, which places them on the front line of traditional stakeholder needs consultation.

Future GSBPM expectation: The modernization agenda transforms this liaison and translation function into an evidence-based, digital consultation workflow, requiring the Coordinator to use machine-actionable metadata platforms to rapidly determine if client needs can be met from assets already available. Further, only when needs clearly cannot be met via current holdings—and following cost-benefit driven, transparent discussions—will new tabulation or data collection proposals advance. Cycles are shortened, and emphasis is placed on maximizing reusability, minimizing burden, and documenting all decision processes.

Role evolution: The Coordinator’s process will need to rely far less on iterative, person-to-person exploratory investigation and more on expert navigation of metadata/discovery platforms, facilitating rapid, value-driven assessments in collaboration with clients. This includes helping stakeholders navigate automated results, surfacing trade-offs transparently, and ensuring that every need assessment is documented and aligned with agency priority and asset availability. The role will also have to respond to and participate in more frequent process feedback and realignment cycles.

Capability implication: This evolution privileges deep operational familiarity with agency metadata, data discovery and exploration platforms, knowledge of how to audit and surface reusability and feasibility of data, and agility in leading clients through digital consultation cycles. The role also grows to require fluency in articulating resource, respondent burden, and value trade-offs in language accessible to non-technical users, as well as proficiency in logging and tracking these decisions for management review.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Identify concepts
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-03 role currently involves providing subject matter advice on statistical concepts, developing or modifying concepts and definitions, and interpreting user requests to determine data needs. This includes 'develops new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques', and 'provides advice to data users and clients on matters relating to subject-matter concepts used in the development and operation of a statistical database.' These activities are typically performed in a manual, expert-driven fashion, based heavily on user requirements and program-specific expertise.

Future GSBPM expectation: The emergence of metadata-driven, AI-assisted tools fundamentally changes the approach to concept identification. The future process places less emphasis on ground-up, ad hoc definition of concepts and instead expects rapid, system-supported discovery, alignment with enterprise standards, and machine-actionable outputs. Human experts are expected to validate, prioritize, and arbitrate rather than generate concepts from scratch.

Role evolution: This role transitions from individually driven, manual curation of concepts and user needs interpretation to orchestrating and overseeing automated concept identification tools. The EC-03 is expected to assess outputs of AI/metadata systems, steer harmonization with enterprise assets, and provide judgment in cases of conceptual alignment, conflict, or gap resolution.

Capability implication: This change increases the importance of understanding enterprise data holdings, metadata standards, AI-based recommendation logic, and the principles of interoperability. The ability to evaluate and arbitrate among system-suggested concepts, ensuring FAIR alignment and program coherence, supersedes the prior focus on manual, bottom-up subject-matter development.
